reason:
As written the falsifier does not discriminate. (1) Regime mismatch: THM_INCBARRIER2 P5.3 says Theorem F needs BIL(theta>=1/4) at coefficient-set sizes < p^{1/2}; Ahmadi-Shparlinski-type bounds already operate at >= p^{1/2+eps}. The toy uses |A|=|B|=p^0.55 (>p^{1/2}), the already-known regime, so a pass says nothing about KN-OPEN-91d4f6. At |A||B|

1). (2) Bound is vacuous at the toy parameters: 3d*p^{-0.05} = 1.5d (p=2^20), 1.4d (2^22), 1.31d (2^24), i.e. 1.3-9.0 for d=1..6; p^{-0.05} barely moves over 2^20..2^24 (0.50 -> 0.43), so 'gain tends to 1' cannot be observed and 'excess >10x bound' requires bucket mass >=14x uniform (only a grossly degenerate filter, not a subtle one). Prediction_if_true and prediction_if_false are not separated by any outcome likely to occur. (3) No null/control arm: hill-climbing over d+1 coefficients in F_p against a fixed sample is selection-biased (max over ~p^{d+1} filters), so excess must be compared to the same hill-climber run on a random-function null of equal bucket density and on held-out (A',B') drawn independently. (4) Interval bases: sums of two intervals {iG}+{jG} give only ~2p^0.55 distinct points (~2^12 at p=2^20, ~16 hits per 1/256 bucket, ~25% noise), so the sample is far noisier than pairs-count |A||B| suggests; and 'random or interval' A,B are two benign points, while the claim is for all A,B (adversarial A,B are the actual Wagner-relevant case). (5) 'excess' is undefined (relative to which density, signed/abs, which normalisation). (6) The sufficient and necessary quantity is the spectral sup norm of F=1[f(x(.))in bucket] over the cyclic group Z/N, because |sum_{P in A,Q in B} F(P+Q) - |A||B|mu| <= lambda*sqrt(|A||B|)*(...) for ALL A,B with lambda=max nontrivial |F^|; bounding lambda by O(d sqrt p) is the DL-twisted character sum problem (sum_k psi(f(x(kG))) e(jk/N)), which is not Weil-accessible and is adjacent to the atlas-closed 'DL character-sum pseudorandomness' / 'coordinate-statistic bias hunts (exhausted at scale)'; the experiment as designed never looks at it. (7) Runtime fine: numpy vectorised at p<=2^24 within 15 CPU-min feasible, no Sage needed; metric is a structural quantity (bucket mass / Fourier coefficient), not wall time. (8) Scaling to p~2^130: toy cannot reach it, but a scaling fit of lambda/sqrt(N) (or log ratio to null) vs log p over p=2^12..2^24 with d fixed is a legitimate trend test; a single p^0.55 point is not. Toy evidence only; no statement about deployed curves.
fix: Replace bilinear sampling with an exact spectral test. For each p in {2^14,2^16,2^18,2^20,2^22} (2^24 if memory allows, ~128MB/array), pick random E/F_p with prime (or large-prime-factor) order N, generate all kG, k=0..N-1, vectorised: baby table iG (i<2^{e/2}) and giant table jH, H=2^{e/2}G, add via batched affine addition with numpy int64 (p<2^24 so products <2^48) and Fermat-inverse by vectorised pow; store x[k]. For each degree d=1..6 and bucket I=[0,p/256): F_f[k]=1[f(x[k]) mod p in I]; compute rfft over k, record (a) lambda_f = max_{j!=0}|F^(j)| / sqrt(N*mu), mu=1/256, (b) the bilinear gain at sub-sqrt(p) sizes via the exact identity sup over A,B of |sum F(P+Q)| bounded by lambda; also directly test adversarial A,B: A=B={k : F_f'(k) high} greedy / top-s sets with |A|=|B|=p^{theta}, theta in {0.25,0.35,0.45,0.55}, plus intervals and uniform-random sets, reporting bucket mass ratio (observed/expected) and its z-score. Arms: (i) real f(x(kG)); (ii) NULL-1: same pipeline with x replaced by a random permutation of the x multiset (kills DL structure, keeps x marginal); (iii) NULL-2: i.i.d. Bernoulli(1/256) mask of same size. Hill-climb f (coefficients in F_p, objective = lambda_f or train-set bucket mass) identically on all arms with identical evaluation budget, then evaluate on held-out independent (A',B') / re-seeded curve; report excess = (real_climbed - null_climbed)/null_sd. Pre-register thresholds: TRUE-supporting if climbed real lambda_f/sqrt(N*mu) within 1.5x of NULL-2 and flat or decreasing in p for every d<=6; FALSE-supporting if real/null ratio >=3 persistently, stable across held-out curves and growing or constant (not shrinking) over p=2^14..2^22 (a fitted slope in log p). Report raw counts (bucket hits, N, lambda) not wall time. Add d=1 sanity check (f=ax+b, x in dilated interval) as known-pseudorandom positive control, and a planted control: inject a filter correlation (e.g. flip bucket membership of a known degree-2 f for a 5% subset) to confirm the pipeline detects an excess of the size claimed in prediction_if_false. Cost: FFT of 2^22 ~ seconds; hill-climb 200 evaluations x 6 d x 3 arms x 5 p ~ under 15 CPU-min at <=2^22. Interpretation limit: toy sees only trend in p; supports/contradicts the claim only at toy scale and does not touch the sub-p^{1/2} regime unless the A,B sizes theta<=0.45 arm is included, which the fix adds.
